rv.q: And since Johnny Byron is portrayed by Mark Rylance, in a seismic performance that threatens to level the old Theater, this registers as utterly natural cause and effect.
Jerusalem is theatre at its visceral, thrilling best.
Rylance’s extraordinary performance turns Jerusalem into a must-see experience for any serious theatergoer.
The play takes wing ever more fleetly on Rylance’s astonishing exertions.
Rylance's deliciously subversive performance triggers both barrels of Butterworth's funny if disconcerting play.
Jez Butterworth's script is far too long, repetitive, and it doesn't need to be to make the point he wants it to make.
Connoisseurs of great acting won't want to miss him—but those with normal attention spans will be hard pressed to make it to the finish line.
It’s to Butterworth’s credit that we are left so conflicted by this meeting with a force of nature, in the best play of the season.

Gusts of national (or is it existential?) pride, fury, despair, and compassion blow through Jez Butterworth's galvanizing drama Jerusalem, imported to Broadway from London's Theatre with star Mark Rylance in brilliant blaze.
Any serious theatergoer who misses an event like this should be bulldozed in favor of condos.
Rylance gives a mesmerizing, thoroughly transformative performance that will leave theatergoers in awe of his spectacular physical and vocal abilities.
The production at the Music Box is bold and high-spirited and boasts terrific acting.
I don't think my problem with 'Jerusalem' is that I don't get it. I just don't buy it.

Considering his brilliant comic turn earlier this season in the revival of La Bete and now his titanic performance in Jez Butterworth’s new play Jerusalem at the same theater, we might as well engrave actor Mark Rylance’s Tony Award right now.
This is an ambitious, iinguistically nervy “State of England” play, funny, amoral, and pungent.

cn.t: Critics largely hail Butterworth's ambitious drama and Rylance's extraordinary performance as unforgettable, though some find the three-hour play pretentious and inaccessible to American audiences.

vs.sum: The Music Box Theatre offers excellent sightlines from most seats, making it ideal for intimate dramas, though sound quality can vary. The theater's charming Georgian-inspired design adds to its ambiance, while comfort and facilities are average for a Broadway venue.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
